# `git merge --squash` fires post-merge even when it conflicted, with the
# conflicts still sitting in the index. Revealing there would overwrite the
# driver's merge result with our side, so the hook keeps its hands off.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

cp base.txt $TMPDIR/base.txt
cp ours.txt $TMPDIR/ours.txt
cp theirs.txt $TMPDIR/theirs.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret'

exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change s'

exec git checkout master
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'master: change s'

! exec git merge --squash topic

# The markers the driver wrote survive the hook.
grep '^<<<<<<< ' s
grep 'OURS' s
grep 'THEIRS' s
exec sesam status
stdout 'conflicted'

-- base.txt --
line one
BASE
line three
-- ours.txt --
line one
OURS
line three
-- theirs.txt --
line one
THEIRS
line three
